analysis: The PR changes only docs/operations/provider-release.md: it bumps the date, updates the release-prep narrative from 0.10.9 to 0.10.10, and replaces the catalog-room and rollout checklist. Base lines 917-1140 and head lines 1-484 were reviewed. The changes are documentation of release procedure, and no source, workflow, or script is modified. The visible head text does not weaken any control. It keeps the explicit human authorization requirement, the signed-tag gate, hash-pinned registration, the trusted-master resolver, the prod-only secrets, and the platform-owned revocation/qualification, all unchanged (lines 97-124, 225-242). The new text documents that registering 0.10.10 omits v0.10.8's derived cluster approvals, because catalog bounds drop the older release. That is an availability and operational consequence for pairs still on 0.10.8, and the document states it deliberately; it is not a security regression. I found no credential exposure, no relaxation of the App Attest, attestation, or cache posture (T-041, TB-011), and no new attack surface. Unverified items: the claims about the platform's catalog bounds and #643 behavior live in the external darkbloom-platform repo and were not supplied, and the patch excerpt is truncated, so the mid-document base changes at base lines 1-916 were not visible. The visible head content is consistent with prior behavior. Nothing here needs a threat-model update.
